primary_purpose: Document, as a reproducible and auditable record, how each defect diagnosed in the 0057 slop artifact was remediated and evolved into a bounded, epistemically-labeled honest harness -- the verifiable slop-to-honest delta (see slop_remediation_map), with the reference run as supporting evidence rather than the headline.
classification_note: QSOT-Harness v2.1.2 (the r1 hardening release) is the honest reconstruction of the QSOT Compiler v1.2.3 slop artifact audited in toe-test-0057. Where 0057 wrapped a flat single-qubit amplitude-damping toy in ungrounded general-relativity nomenclature (with KD negativity and TTM non-Markovianity evaluating to exactly 0.0), 0059 makes the model's epistemic status machine-readable: a fixed claim boundary, a per-observation evidence class, environment-dependent backend surfacing, a calibration manifest, and a strict separation of detector self-tests from model-generated signals. The run is verified for model-output consistency only.

new_slop_pattern_caught.description: A placeholder reference (LeeFullwood2025) carried specific Physical Review Letters coordinates (vol 134, p.100401, 2025) while the prose called it a 'conceptual placeholder', and its title contained the project's own internal acronym expansion ('Quantum Geometry Bridge'). Specific bibliographic coordinates on a self-described placeholder, plus a title echoing the project's own jargon, are strong fabrication signals.
new_slop_pattern_caught.detection: Independent web verification found no such paper; the real adjacent work is by James Fullwood (different title/journal).
new_slop_pattern_caught.remediation: Removed and replaced with the verified Pikovski et al. 2015, Nature Physics 11:668-672 (DOI 10.1038/nphys3366), cited inspiration-only with an explicit non-derivation disclaimer.
new_slop_pattern_caught.reusable_lesson: Treat specific journal/volume/page coordinates attached to a 'placeholder' or 'inspiration' reference as a fabrication red flag; verify externally before publication.
